diagnosis: The gate failed because rollout 1 was the sole failing rollout, and it failed exclusively on check C1 (furnace_sequence). In that rollout, all four decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4) were properly revealed by their owners and correctly cited in justification_fact_ids, but the model settled on sequence "R → P → Q" instead of the expected "R, Q, P". PF3 was revealed by A4 and cited as justification, yet C1 still failed — this is an ENCODING MISMATCH. PF3 only constrains R to be first (the 4-hour oxidation limit), but C1 demands the exact full sequence R-Q-P, including the Q-before-P ordering that no decisive fact actually constrains. The model reasonably placed R first but saw no information distinguishing Q-vs-P order, so it sometimes chose P before Q.

C1.why: The four-hour oxidation limit changes the sequence to R-Q-P, and only this fact explains why batch R must be scheduled first.

fix_instructions: The sole failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH on check C1. PF3 was revealed and cited in all 4 rollouts, but C1 failed in rollout 1 because it requires the exact sequence "R, Q, P" while PF3 only establishes that R must be first. Fix by either (a) relaxing C1 to verify only that R is the first batch in the sequence (matching what PF3 actually constrains), or (b) if the full R-Q-P ordering is genuinely required, add a fifth decisive fact owned by an appropriate agent that constrains Q before P (e.g., a material readiness or customer deadline for batch Q), and add a corresponding content check gated on that new fact. No changes are needed to PF1, PF2, PF4, or checks C2–C7 and P1, which passed in all 4 rollouts.
